faq.a: Juma is associated with the Arabic form جُمْعَة, whose core sense is juma; born on friday (swahili form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Juma?
faq.a: Juma is associated with Arabic. Juma is the Swahili form of Arabic جُمْعَة (Jumʿa, 'Friday'), used for a child born on Friday.
Yes — the underlying form جُمْعَة is Arabic.
Juma can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Juma should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Jumʿa is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Juma mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Juma is rendered جمعہ and carries the sense جمعہ، جمعہ کے دن پیدا ہوا.

faq.q: What does Juma mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Juma is rendered جمعه and carries the sense جمعه، زاده جمعه.
A romanized syllable approximation is ju-ma. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Juma?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Juma, juma. Script forms are جمعه, جمعہ, جُمْعَة, जुमा.

faq.q: Is Juma a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
